newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks surge after Fed holds rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks surge after Fed holds rates steady.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks raced higher for the second day in a row on Tuesday after the Federal Reserve elected to hold interest rates steady.
The dollar also rallied, while gasoline prices surged amid concern about low inventories.
Stocks rose sharply as the Fed's decision to stand pat on interest rates added more spark to the market's fiery recovery from last Friday's plunge.
The Dow Jones industrial average climbed 114.74 points, or 1.47 percent, to 7,918.10 after storming 109 points higher on Monday on the back of Friday's 247-point loss.
The Nasdaq composite index jumped 31.19 points, or nearly 2 percent, at 1,600.71 on the strength of technology stocks.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped decliners 2,026 to 804 on a heavy volume of 545 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Wall Street cheered the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged, which was seen as a vote of confidence that the economy can continue to grow at a comfortable speed without reigniting inflation.

"The Fed did nothing today, and my guess is that they're not going to do anything probably through the end of the year," said Lawrence Chimerine, managing director at the Economic Strategy Institute, a Washington-based think tank.

The central bank last raised rates on March 25, when it boosted the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, a move that sparked a sell-off of nearly 10 percent in the blue-chip Dow index. The Fed has since held the line on interest rates.

In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 4/32, or $1.25 on a $1,000 bond, trimming its yield to 6.51 percent from 6.52 percent on Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Technology stocks sizzled as money managers, looking for more growth and cheaper valuations, rotated money out of blue-chip stocks and into the high-tech sector, analysts said.
"Most of the blue chips have had such strong advances, how much further can they go? The play is to look for growth," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage.
The dollar rose after the German central bank elected to leave interest rates unchanged. The sharp rebound in the stock market also aided the U.S. currency.
The dollar closed at 1.8405 German marks, up a full pfennig from 1.8305 marks on Monday. It also edged up to 118.20 Japanese yen from 117.82 yen on Monday.
Elsewhere, gasoline prices rose as traders bet that weekly oil industry inventory figures would show a sharp drawdown in gasoline stocks.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, gasoline for September delivery rose 2.14 cents a gallon to 67.58 cents. After the close of trading, the American Petroleum Institute reported that U.S. gasoline stocks fell 3.3 million barrels to just under 188 million barrels for the week ended August 15.
Overseas, Britain's FTSE 100 rose 79.2 points, or 1.64 percent, to 4,914.2. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 18,961.00, down 80.10 points, or 0.42 percent.
